title: The Third Declension — Vowel and σ-Stems
subtitle: ἡ πόλις, ὁ βασιλεύς, τὸ γένος — lengthening and contraction.
objectives: Decline third-declension ι-stems, ευ-stems, and εσ-stems in all cases.
Recognize compensatory lengthening when σ drops between vowels.
Parse πόλις, βασιλεύς, and γένος on sight.
Understand the contraction patterns in neuter εσ-stems.

sections.heading: Vowel and σ-stems
sections.body:
Some third-declension nouns have stems ending in vowels (ι, υ) or in sigma. The sigma often drops between vowels, and the resulting vowels contract or lengthen.

πόλις (city) has the stem πολι-. βασιλεύς (king) has the stem βασιλευ-. γένος (race, kind) has the stem γενεσ-, but the σ drops in most forms.

These nouns show compensatory lengthening: when a consonant drops, the preceding vowel lengthens. ε + dropping σ + vowel often produces a long vowel or diphthong.

sections.heading: ι-stems: ἡ πόλις (city)
sections.body:
Stem: πολι-
              singular        plural
  nominative  πόλις           πόλεις
  genitive    πόλεως          πόλεων
  dative      πόλει           πόλεσι(ν)
  accusative  πόλιν           πόλεις
  vocative    πόλι            πόλεις

The genitive and dative singular show lengthening: πόλι + ος → πόλεως (ι lengthens to ε + compensatory lengthening).

sections.heading: ευ-stems: ὁ βασιλεύς (king)
sections.body:
Stem: βασιλευ-
              singular        plural
  nominative  βασιλεύς        βασιλεῖς
  genitive    βασιλέως        βασιλέων
  dative      βασιλεῖ         βασιλεῦσι(ν)
  accusative  βασιλέα         βασιλέας
  vocative    βασιλεῦ         βασιλεῖς

The nominative plural contracts ευ + ες → εῖς. The accusative singular loses the υ: βασιλέα.

sections.heading: εσ-stems: τὸ γένος (race, kind)
sections.body:
Stem: γενεσ- (the σ drops between vowels)
              singular        plural
  nominative  γένος           γένη
  genitive    γένους          γενῶν
  dative      γένει           γένεσι(ν)
  accusative  γένος           γένη
  vocative    γένος           γένη

The genitive singular γένους comes from γενεσ-ος → γενε(σ)ος → γένους (ε + ο contracts to ου). The nominative/accusative plural γένη comes from γενεσ-α → γένε(σ)α → γένη (ε + α contracts to η).

items.answer: When a consonant drops, the preceding vowel lengthens to compensate.

sections.heading: Up next
sections.body: Lesson 3.9 introduces adjectives of the third declension: ἀληθής, εὐδαίμων, πᾶς. These adjectives follow third-declension patterns and can be mixed (third declension in masculine and neuter, first declension in feminine).

lesson_completion.criteria: Mark the lesson complete when you can decline πόλις, βασιλεύς, and γένος from memory and can explain compensatory lengthening and contraction in these nouns.
